fieldMarks: Male black at both ends and whitish in the middle; often a purple gloss on the head in good light
Female brown-headed with a white face patch
Peak at the back of the crown and slightly smaller bill than greater scaup
White wing stripe reaches only about halfway out the wing
behavior: Very active diver, surfacing repeatedly; sometimes feeds at night
Winters in dense single-species flocks of hundreds or thousands
Eats mostly mollusks, aquatic insects and crustaceans plus aquatic plants; on the Great Lakes may feed heavily on zebra mussels
Migrates in flocks late in fall and early in spring
habitat: Summers around large marshes in prairie or forest; winters on lakes, reservoirs, rivers and sheltered coastal bays, far more often inland on fresh water than greater scaup.
range: Breeds from central Alaska and the Mackenzie Delta to northern Manitoba and northern Ontario south to southern British Columbia, northern Idaho, North Dakota and Minnesota; winters from southern British Columbia and the southern Great Lakes and New England south through the southern U.S. to Central America.

lookalikes.name: Greater scaup
lookalikes.howToTell: Head shape is the best mark: lesser has a peaked rear crown, smaller bill and a white wing stripe only half the wing's length.
